simple: Demand is the quantity of a good that buyers are willing and able to purchase at a given price.
examples: For example, when the price of coffee went from three dollars to five dollars at the campus cafe, daily sales dropped by almost half.
apply: Explain how Demand would show up in a real situation, in your own words.

simple: The law of demand is the principle that, all else equal, quantity demanded falls as price rises.
apply: Explain how Law of Demand would show up in a real situation, in your own words.

simple: Supply is the quantity of a good that producers are willing to sell at a given price.
examples: For example, when coffee prices rose, two new roasters entered the market because selling coffee became more profitable.
apply: Explain how Supply would show up in a real situation, in your own words.

simple: Equilibrium is the price at which the quantity buyers want exactly equals the quantity sellers offer.
apply: Explain how Equilibrium would show up in a real situation, in your own words.

simple: A shortage is the situation where quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at the current price.
examples: For instance, during the shortage last spring, the bookstore ran out of calculators in the first week.
apply: Explain how Shortage would show up in a real situation, in your own words.

simple: A surplus is the situation where quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at the current price.
apply: Explain how Surplus would show up in a real situation, in your own words.

simple: Elasticity is a measure of how strongly quantity demanded or supplied responds to a change in price.
examples: For example, demand for insulin is nearly unchanging when its price rises, while demand for concert tickets falls quickly.
apply: Explain how Elasticity would show up in a real situation, in your own words.
